lena (android): heads-up: onboarding sample app sees uploads drop Authorization header after a 307 redirect + auth refresh. Only on Android 12+ devices.

mike (sdk): interesting. is the 307 coming from our CDN or from the API? 307 should preserve method/body per spec but OkHttp has quirks.

lena (android): CDN returns 307 to a presigned upload url. flow: POST /v1/upload -> 307 -> direct S3-like url. Our Authenticator refreshes token and retries original request, but after redirect the final request to the presigned host loses Authorization header and fails with 403.

omar (eng-runtime): likely ordering: Redirects happen at network layer after Authenticator injection; if Authenticator mutates the request at retry time and OkHttp performs redirect to a different host, `Authorization` is removed unless `Intercept` re-adds it. Also streaming bodies are non-repeatable so OkHttp might convert to GET on redirect in some cases.

mike (sdk): can you paste the Interceptor/Authenticator minimalist flow?

lena (android): simplified: 
```
// network interceptor
chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer " + TokenStore.get()).build();
// Authenticator does blocking refresh and returns request with new header
```

mike (sdk): two quick notes: 1) OkHttp strips `Authorization` when redirecting to a different host by default — that's a security feature. 2) If your Authenticator returns a request for the original URL, OkHttp will still perform the redirect step and may not copy headers across.

omar (eng-runtime): mitigation: a) use pre-signed upload URL as a separate call (do not rely on following redirect paths inside the same call) b) when you get 307, handle it in app: follow redirect manually and preserve headers you intend to send (but be careful). c) shorter: attach Authorization in an application-level interceptor (not network interceptor) so it is reapplied for retried requests.

lena (android): note that app-level interceptor runs before Authenticator? we rely on network interceptor to avoid tampering.

mike (sdk): order: application interceptors run before redirects and are invoked for every follow-up request; network interceptors run around the network stack and might not be re-run for redirects. So prefer application interceptor for auth header injection.

lena (android): thanks. quick patch: moved header injection to application interceptor and added explicit handling for 307 to treat it as special case (do not forward to OkHttp followRedirects). Repro on device fixed.

ci-bot: CI run for branch fix/redirect-auth-218001 passed e2e.

mike (sdk): follow-up: we'll add a small note to DX docs about redirect host header stripping and sample showing application-level auth interceptor + presigned upload pattern. Also add a small test for 307->presigned flow.

lena (android): will open PR with sample and a short blurb in onboarding README. thanks :thumbsup:
